So yeah, as the title says? How did you guys get into MMA?

For me it started when I was a kid in the 90's. I was a huge pro wrestling fan, and my dad would order big boxing PPVs or take me to watch some with friends. During the mid-90's I would always go to the local Blockbuster to rent WWF tapes. They were always at the back on the right hand side of the front entrance. I would always go there before going to the video game section. One day in 1997 before Ken Shamrock debuted on Raw, I saw a UFC tape next to the WWF tapes and checked it out. I liked it even though I didn't know much about it, but my dad thought ti was trash, so he never let me rent UFC tapes.

Years go by, I'm still into wrestling. Ken Shamrock, Dan Severn, and Tank Abbott kept MMA/UFC on the back of my mind. Around 2002 a friend of mine and I watched Chuck Liddell vs. Vitor Belfort on "The Best Damn Sports Show Period" and after that his dad ordered UFC 40. Didn't watch anything else until the first TUF Finale and sorta resented it because of the Bonnar/Griffin. I did love watching fighting, be it street fights, boxing, whatever, but wasn't into the UFC cause of guys like Griffin and Leben. Pride had a run on Fox Sports Net, but it didn't really capture the atmosphere of Pride since the shows I saw were compilation shows.

But then came Anderson Silva's UFC debut, EliteXC debuting on CBS, WEC on Versus, the rise of Strikeforce, and Hendo's KO of Michael Bisping. Throw in the fact that pro-wrestling began to suck and boxing was getting stale at the time, it had me starting to go back and watch tapes/DVDs and becoming obsessed with MMA.

tl:dr - Watched a UFC tape as kid, watched UFC on FSN and UFC 40 in 2002, hated TUF, Anderson Silva, EliteXC, and stuff.

My story is a lot like yours.

When I was a kid, I was into WWF wrestling in a big way (thats right, not WWE) and used to watch it often with my uncle. We went to a few events here and there and I met Hulk Hogan and a few other people.

As I grew up, my brother and I got into all kinds of things like motocross and racing and various other stuff, we eventually watched a few pretty badass compilation tapes our step dad had that featured "extreme" sports which was in addition to motocross etc. various fighting events like Sambo and Muay Thai. Around this time we were also in the habit of renting video games / movies from corner stores, Blockbuster etc. and at one point I remember seeing amongst the WWE tapes was various compilation tapes for extreme sports etc. Eventually I noticed a UFC tape (UFC 2) and rented it along with various other movies.

After we popped that in and saw what it was, we lost our fucking minds. This was like Bloodsport and Kickboxer and all the other movies we were huge fans of already, except it was real! So we immediately set out to rent/acquire as much of this stuff as possible and ended up watching the first few events this way and made sure to request them at the local stores. As we grew up, my step brother stayed interested in wrestling but got into the more foreign shit like ECW and japanese wrestling whereas I on the other hand stayed into MMA and Boxing. Later on this morphed into watching Pride and K-1 and the UFC once it returned to television.

From then on I've basically watched every event I can, I watched everything Pride ever did, the first few seasons of TUF (though honestly I got bored of it pretty quickly as the caliber of fights was meh for the most part) and continue to this day to watch and follow the sport more than anything else (though Hockey does take up a fair amount of my time during the season).

I don't see myself ever disliking MMA, having really grown up with the sport and guys like Rogan and Goldie as well as seeing various fight camps from their very beginnings, it's just grown to be something I love and is a regular part of my life.
